keyframe_review.note: 1569: Aki Kunitora beaten at Yanagare and Aki Castle taken, 'extending his power in east Tosa' (Motochika page). A 22 km circle at Aki is the researcher's reading.
1575: 'Victory at the Battle of Watarigawa gave him the rest of Tosa' (clan page; the Ichijō were overthrown in 1574). Kōchi Prefecture (32 cells, about 8,100 km2) stands for Tosa.

1580: Motochika 'led about 30,000 men into Iyo' and forced Kōno Michinao to flee to Bungo (Motochika page). Ehime Prefecture (26 cells) stands for Iyo; the page does not say all of Iyo was held (the 1583 sentence says he 'controlled Tosa and Iyo').
1582: Sogō Masayasu and the Miyoshi beaten at Nakatomigawa (Awa).

1583: Sengoku Hidehisa beaten at Hiketa (Sanuki); the Shikoku page: 'controlled Iyo, Sanuki, Awa, and Tosa'; the Motochika page: Tosa and Iyo held, Awa and Sanuki 'subdued'; the clan page: all of Shikoku in 1583. The four prefectures (92 cells) stand for the island.
6 August 1585: 'Chōsokabe was allowed to keep Tosa Province' after losing Awa, Sanuki and Iyo. 'After 1600, the Chōsokabe were removed as daimyō of Tosa' (clan page).

1569: 'Defeated Aki Kunitora at Yanagare and took Aki Castle, extending his power in east Tosa.'

union.text: the Kōchi plain in central Tosa

ledger.note: 1575: the Battle of Shimantogawa (Watarigawa) 'gave him the rest of Tosa'; the clan page also has the Ichijō overthrown in 1574 and the Motochika page the attack on their Nakamura headquarters in 1573, Ichijō Kanesada fleeing to Bungo.
1580: 'led about 30,000 men into Iyo' and forced Kōno Michinao to flee to Bungo (1579: his commander Kumu Yorinobu killed at Mimaomote). The extent of the holding is the researcher's reading.
1582: 'Defeated Sogō Masayasu and the Miyoshi clan at the Battle of Nakatomigawa.' The page says Awa was 'subdued'.
1583: 'Defeated Sengoku Hidehisa at the Battle of Hiketa.' The page says Sanuki was 'subdued'.
June 1585: Hideyoshi assembled 113,000 men in three armies; Chōsokabe had about 40,000 to defend Shikoku.
6 August 1585 (11th day of the 7th month of Tenshō 13): Chōsokabe surrendered after the 26-day siege of Ichinomiya.
6 August 1585: Awa, Sanuki and Iyo lost, to Hachisuka Iemasa and Akamatsu Norifusa (Awa), Sengoku Hidehisa and Sogō Masayasu (Sanuki), Kobayakawa Takakage and other Mōri generals (Iyo).

After 1600: 'the Chōsokabe were removed as daimyō of Tosa'; Morichika had led the clan's forces for the Toyotomi at Sekigahara. The page names no actor and no month; the winning side's lord is the researcher's naming of the counterpart. The clan itself ended after the Siege of Osaka (1615), when Morichika was executed (infobox: ruled until 1615).

wars.name: Chōsokabe conquest of Tosa
wars.outcome: The Motoyama fell in 1560, the Aki in 1569, the Ichijō in 1574-1575 (Watarigawa); Tosa was Chōsokabe's.

wars.name: Chōsokabe campaigns in Iyo, Awa and Sanuki
wars.outcome: Iyo 1580, Awa 1582 (Nakatomigawa), Sanuki 1583 (Hiketa); by 1583 all Shikoku.

wars.name: Invasion of Shikoku
wars.outcome: Chōsokabe surrendered on 6 August 1585 and kept Tosa; Awa, Sanuki and Iyo were taken.

wars.name: Sekigahara campaign (Chōsokabe side)
wars.outcome: Morichika led the clan's forces for the Toyotomi; after 1600 the Chōsokabe were removed as daimyo of Tosa.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from three pages (Chōsokabe clan, Chōsokabe Motochika, Invasion of Shikoku). A Sengoku daimyo domain inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row. Dated by the pages: eastern Tosa (1569), the rest of Tosa (1574-1575), Iyo (1580), Awa (1582), Sanuki (1583), the loss of the three (6 August 1585), the removal after 1600. Page conflicts: the clan page says Motochika 'extended his power over all of Shikoku' in 1583, the Motochika page that he held Tosa and Iyo in 1583 and had 'subdued' Awa and Sanuki, extending to all Shikoku 'over the following decade'; the clan page gives about 100,000 men for Hideyoshi in 1585, the Shikoku and Motochika pages 113,000; the Motochika page puts Nobuchika's death at Hetsugigawa (Kyushu, 1586-1587) while the clan page names no battle. The clan page's infobox says 'ruled until 1615, Battle of Osaka'; this dossier ends at 1600, when Tosa was lost. Not on the pages: who received Tosa after 1600, the Chōsokabe seat (Ōkō or Urado), the Kōno and Ichijō land extents. The Toyotomi dossier carries Tosa as a vassal tint from 1585 (bridging end 1600). Counterpart strings: 'toyotomi-clan' exists; the others are persons or clans named on the pages. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
